scope: Independently authored fake ACP process and synthetic protocol cases; no live conversation captures
constraints: No imports from proxy implementation packages
fixture/* methods are synthetic test controls, not Kiro capabilities
Prepared-launch markers and alias manifests are invented fixture controls, not copied Kiro configuration or effective restriction evidence
All text, error strings, IDs and credential sentinels are synthetic
Descendant processes only exercise lifecycle cleanup; they execute no client tool
The chat-tools-separate-group mode deliberately creates an MCP child in a distinct process group for the independent cooperative group-join experiment
The chat-tools-stopped-idle mode stops only its own relay PID after a synthetic result, testing bounded cleanup failure and process retirement without a client tool effect
Effort command shapes remain specification interpretations under D09; the separate read-only tools inventory uses the observed D39 envelope with independently authored data

Inventory modes accept only initialization, one session/new and one advertised argument-free tools query; optional MCP readiness must match the owned session and exact serverName; no model prompt or tool effect is supported
Independent multi-server inventory cases distinguish exact declared sources, a missing source and a delayed post-reply readiness notification
The other-cwd inventory case requires the exact independently supplied session directory and checks that its inode differs from the fake process working directory
Catalog inventory cases provide independent matching, mismatching and malformed session model state; no model selector or prompt call is supported
The chat-tools-client-launch case combines an independently supplied relay launch manifest with one Read request and requires the synthetic client-hook denial before its sole ACP prompt completes
MCP tool requests are answered by synthetic test clients or an opt-in unmodified public client with independently authored permission rules and hooks; the fake backend does not execute client tools

The chat-tools-effect-launch case reads only the owned request/expectation manifest, relays one exact argument object and validates its returned status/content before completion; only the public client reads/writes the separate effect file or executes the specified shell command
The native-control peer verifies empty ACP capabilities, one inventory/model selection/prompt, rejection of permission/filesystem/terminal requests, and terminal completion

Native observer contamination controls deliberately create one synthetic marker or read and emit an owned random canary; these are independent test instrumentation that must fail the isolation observer, never real user data or client tool execution
Other native controls supply a foreign session, tool status, absent text, cancelled stop reason or silent turn to prevent those outcomes from counting as restriction proof

The chat-tools-recovery-launch peer accepts one full prompt with empty prior history, the exact new synthetic question and native standing context; it rejects the old target path and returns only independent fixed text

The process-loss harness terminates only its observed owned ACP group before the pending Read reaches the client; no captured live prompt, model text or previous implementation is an input to the recovery fixture
